span.label: method
span.quote: In this paper, we review variational inference (VI), a method from machine learning that approximates probability densities through optimization.

span.label: variational inference for approximate posterior densities
span.quote: One of the core problems of modern statistics is to approximate difficult-to-compute probability densities.

span.label: review
span.quote: In this paper, we review variational inference (VI), a method from machine learning for approximating probability densities (Jordan et al., 1999; Wainwright and Jordan, 2008).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: recast posterior inference as optimization: choose the distribution in a simple (mean-field) family that is closest in KL divergence to the true posterior, via coordinate ascent
span.quote: closest in KL divergence to the conditional of interest

span.label: VI has been studied less rigorously than MCMC and its statistical properties are less well understood
span.quote: But variational inference has been studied less rigorously than MCMC, and its statistical properties are less well understood.

span.label: The authors state that variational inference is not yet theoretically well understood.
span.quote: VI is powerful, but it is not yet well understood.

span.label: The paper's comparison against MCMC is not definitive; other samplers might perform better.
span.quote: This is not a definitive comparison between variational inference and MCMC.

span.label: Collapsed variational inference is explicitly excluded from the review's scope.
span.quote: These ideas are outside the scope of our review.

span.label: The review deliberately restricts itself to the mean-field family, excluding richer variational families.
span.quote: In this review we focus on the mean-field variational family, where the latent variables are mutually independent and each governed by a distinct factor in the variational density.

span.label: Collapsed variational inference and related speed-ups are excluded from the review's coverage.
span.quote: These ideas are outside the scope of our review.

span.label: The survey of applications is not exhaustive.
span.quote: This discussion is not exhaustive; our intention is to outline the diversity of applications of variational inference.

span.label: The accuracy of variational inference relative to MCMC is not known, and VI is known to underestimate posterior variance.
span.quote: The relative accuracy of variational inference and MCMC is still unknown.

span.label: Variational inference systematically underestimates posterior variance because of its objective function.
span.quote: We do know that variational inference generally underestimates the variance of the posterior density; this is a consequence of its objective function.

span.label: The paper's empirical CAVI-versus-Hamiltonian-Monte-Carlo timing comparison is not a definitive comparison of the two paradigms.
span.quote: Other samplers, such as a collapsed Gibbs sampler, may perform better than Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling.

span.label: The statistical theory of variational inference remains undeveloped, which the paper flags as an open problem rather than something it settles.
span.quote: Finally, the statistical properties of variational inference are not yet well understood, especially in contrast to the wealth of analysis of MCMC techniques.

span.label: The review states that its own subject is not yet well understood, and that its statistical properties have been studied less rigorously than the alternative it is compared to.
span.quote: But variational inference has been studied less rigorously than MCMC, and its statistical properties are less well understood.

span.label: The defect is known, directional, and declared possibly acceptable — the acceptability depending on the task rather than on the method.
span.quote: We do know that variational inference generally underestimates the variance of the posterior density; this is a consequence of its objective function. But, depending on the task at hand, underestimating the variance may be acceptable.

span.label: How accurate the method is relative to the alternative is stated to be unknown.
span.quote: The relative accuracy of variational inference and MCMC is still unknown.

span.label: The objective actually optimised is a substitute for the one wanted, adopted because the wanted one cannot be computed.
span.quote: Because we cannot compute the KL, we optimize an alternative objective that is equivalent to the KL up to an added constant

span.label: The optimisation reaches a local optimum only, the objective is generally non-convex, and different initialisations were observed to reach different values.
span.quote: The ELBO is (generally) a non-convex objective function. CAVI only guarantees convergence to a local optimum, which can be sensitive to initialization.

span.label: The monitoring quantity the review recommends in practice lacks the guarantee that belongs to the quantity it stands in for.
span.quote: Monitoring changes here is a proxy to monitoring the ELBO of the full data. (Unlike the full ELBO, held-out predictive probability is not guaranteed to monotonically increase across iterations of CAVI.)

span.quote: Several lines of empirical research have shown that variational inference does not necessarily suffer in accuracy, e.g., in terms of posterior predictive densities
